| 🪢 Tangle · [q-0037.0013](docs/questions/q-0037.0013-how-does-each-turn-know-its-next-step-and-each-session-where-to-resume.md) · [q-0037.0012.0009](docs/questions/q-0037.0012.0009-how-is-an-amendment-to-an-instruction-tested-before-it-lands-against-which-cases-chosen-how-run-with-no-instruction-the-standing-one-and-the-new-one.md) · — · — |
|---|

| 📍 **q-0037.0013** · How does each turn know its next step, and each session where to resume? |
|---|

You do. The order is yours, said in your words and written by hand into the queue, and no mechanism computes it. The answer is already in the tree, so nothing was opened for it.

**What decides a place in the order.** The rule you set on 2026-09-07: the harness is self-building, so the governing consideration is which slice hands the next one a tool that makes the harness work better. A slice that only describes something ranks below one that gives the next slice a script, a check or a rule to lean on. Dependency order and size do not decide it on their own (💡 [*How this queue is ordered*](docs/tickets/README.md:16)). Every later reordering in the queue's narrative carries your name and a date, which is how the record shows whose the order is.

**What the agent does with it.** `/recall` reads the next item from the order as the queue states it and never re-ranks. It only names the occasions for a reordering, a dependency or status the order has come to contradict, a priority that changed, a split a resolution found, and puts each to you (💡 [*Read the next item from the order the queue states*](.claude/skills/recall/SKILL.md:19)). The live ticket list is read before anyone orders, so the order is set over what exists, not over memory. A ticket's own dependencies constrain where it can stand, but they do not choose among what is ready.

**What the queue is, mechanically.** A document that informs: it reaches the work only through the skill that reads it, which is `/recall`, and it authorizes nothing by itself (💡 [*A document informs*](AGENTS.md:25)). The ticket mechanism lists ordering the queue and writing its pacing prose as a part it does not yet have (💡 [*ordering the queue and writing its pacing prose*](.agents/mechanisms/ticket/ticket.md:67)); the pacer, which is [01-0020 each-turn-knows-its-next-step](docs/tickets/01-0020-each-turn-knows-its-next-step.md), is to own it once it exists. Until then the order is applied by hand, by you.
